subject: Future Tech
title: Carbon Nanotubes
description: A short lesson to help you apply Carbon Nanotubes.

hook.text: Carbon nanotubes are 100 times stronger than steel at one-sixth the weight.

buildup.text: A nanotube is a sheet of carbon atoms rolled into a cylinder 1 nm wide. The structure gives it extraordinary properties.

discovery.text: Nanotubes conduct electricity better than copper and heat better than diamond.

twist.text: Making long, defect-free nanotubes is incredibly hard. Most are short and tangled.

climax.text: Despite challenges, nanotubes are already used in tennis rackets, bike frames, and battery electrodes.

punchline.text: The strongest material on Earth is invisible to the naked eye.

quiz.question: How do carbon nanotubes compare to steel in strength?
